89:1: This is an oath by which our Lord, may He be glorified and praised, swears by the dawn, which is the dawn of morning. The interpreters differed about who was meant by this. Some of them said: It meant the day. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Aghar Al-Manqari, on the authority of Khalifa bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and the dawn, he said: the day. Others said: He meant the dawn prayer. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My father told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas: And the dawn means the morning prayer. Others said: It is the dawn of morning. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Asim al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, and the dawn, he said: The accusative is the dawn of the morning. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Umar ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said: And the dawn. He said: The dawn is an oath by which God swore.
89:2: And His statement: And ten nights. The people of interpretation differed regarding these ten nights, which nights they are. Some of them said: They are the first ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Bishr told us, he said: Ibn Abi Udayy, Abd al-Wahhab, and Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The ten nights by which God swore are the first ten nights of that Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday, Abd al-Wahhab, and Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Zurarah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He said: The ten nights by which God swore are the first ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, my uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And ten nights are the ten days of Eid al-Adha. He said: It is said that the ten days are the first of the year from Muharram. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Umar ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Murtafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, And ten nights or Dhul-Hijjah until the Day of Sacrifice. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Aouf told us, he said: Zararah ibn Awfa told us, he said: Ibn Abbas said: The ten nights that God swore by are the first nights of Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Masruq: And ten nights are the ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah, which are the ones that God promised Moses, peace be upon him. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Asim al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, And ten nights, he said: The ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihr told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Aghar Al-Manqari, on the authority of Khalifa bin Husayn, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And ten nights. He said: The ten days of Eid Al-Adha. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And ten nights, he said: the ten of Dhul-Hijjah. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And ten nights. He said: We used to say that they were the ten days of Eid al-Adha. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: There is no deed done during any of the nights of the year that is better than it is during the nights of the ten, which are the ten of Moses that God completed for him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Masuq, who said: The nights of the ten, he said: They are the best days of the year. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And ten nights, meaning the ten days of Eid Al-Adha. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement, And ten nights, he said: The first of Dhul-Hijjah, and he said: They are the ten days of Muharram from its beginning. The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is that they are the ten days of Eid al-Adha, due to the consensus of the jurists among the people of interpretation on this, and that: Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani said: Zaid bin Habbab told me, he said: Ayyash bin Uqbah told me, he said: Jubayr bin Na’im told me on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the dawn and ten nights. He said: The ten days of Eid al-Adha.
89:3: And his saying: And the even and the odd. The people of interpretation differed as to what he meant by the odd in his saying and the odd. Some of them said: The even is the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd is the Day of Arafah. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday, Abd al-Wahhab, and Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Zararah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The witr is the day of Arafah, and the shafa` is the day of sacrifice. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Aouf told us: Zararah ibn Awfa told us: Ibn Abbas said: The even number is the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd number is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Bashar told us: Affan bin Muslim told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ikrimah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The even number is the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd number is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Ikrimah: And the even and the odd. He said: The even is the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd is the Day of Arafah. He told us about it again, and said: The even number is the days of sacrifice, and the rest of the hadith is similar. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Asim al-Ahwal told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, and the even, he said: The Day of Sacrifice, and the odd, he said: The Day of Arafah. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The even is the day of sacrifice and the odd is the day of Arafah. He said: Mihr narrated to us on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, And ten nights * and the even and the odd. He said: God swore by them because He knows of their superiority over all other days, and these two days are better because He knows of their superiority over all other nights. and the even and the odd. He said: The even is the Day of Sacrifice and the odd is the Day of Arafah. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Ikrimah used to say: The even is the day of Eid al-Adha, and the odd is the day of Arafah. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ikrimah said: Arafah is odd, and the sacrifice is even. Arafah is on the ninth day, and the sacrifice is on the tenth day. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the even refers to the Day of Sacrifice, and and the odd refers to the Day of Arafah. Others said: Shafa’ is the two days after the Day of Sacrifice, and Witr is the third day. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, and the even and the odd, he said: The even are two days after the Day of Sacrifice, and the odd is the last day of departure. God says: “But whoever hastens to do so within two days, there is no sin upon him. And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him” (al-Baqarah 2:203). Others said: All of creation, and the string is God. Mention who said that. Muhammad ibn Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father Ibn Abbas: And the even and the odd. He said: God is odd and you are even. It is said that the even is the dawn prayer and the odd is the sunset prayer. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the even and the odd he said: All of God’s creation is even, the heavens and the earth, the land and the sea, the jinn and mankind, the sun and the moon, and God alone is odd. Ya'qub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, he said: Mujahid said regarding His statement, And of everything We have created pairs (al-Dhariyat 51:49): Disbelief and faith, happiness and misery, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, jinn and mankind, and odd. He said: And he said something similar about even and odd. Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me, he said: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, he said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, and the even and the odd, he said: God created of everything in pairs, and God is One, Odd, Eternal. Muhammad bin Amara told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid: And the even and the odd. He said: The even is the pair, and the odd is God. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Mujahid: And the even and the odd. He said: The odd is God, and whatever God created is even. Others said: He meant by that creation, and that is because all creation is even and odd. He said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and the even and the odd, he said: All of creation is even and odd, and He swore by creation. He said: Ibn Thaur narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said about that: All creation is even, and the even and the odd. He said: My father used to say: Everything God created is even and odd, so He swore by what He created, and He swore by what you see and by what you do not see. Others said: Rather, it is the obligatory prayer, including the Shafa’, such as the Fajr and Dhuhr prayers, and the Witr, such as the Maghrib prayer. Mention who said that. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Imran bin Husayn used to say: The even and the odd means the prayer. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: and the even and the odd. Imran said: It is the obligatory prayer in which there are the even and the odd. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Ar-Rabi` ibn Anas: And the even and the odd. He said: This is the Maghrib prayer. The even are the two rak`ahs, and the odd is the third rak`ah. Some have attributed the hadith of Imran ibn Husayn to the Prophet. Who said that? Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: My father told me, he said: Khalid bin Qais told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Imran bin Issam, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the even and the odd, he said: It is the prayer, some of it is even and some of it is odd. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Affan bin Muslim told us, he said: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, that he was asked about the even and the odd, so he said: Imran bin Issam Al-Dab’i told me, on the authority of a sheikh from the people of Basra, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It is the prayer, some of it is even and some of it is odd. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ubayd God ibn Musa told us, he said: Huma ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Imran ibn Issam, on the authority of a sheikh from the people of Basra, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding this verse, ‘and the even and the odd.’ He said: It is the prayer, some of it is even and some of it is odd.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, and his statement, and the even and the odd, that some prayers are even, and some are odd. Ibn Bashar told us: Affan ibn Muslim told us: Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatada, that he was asked about the even and odd numbers, and he said: Al-Hasan said: It is the number. A report was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that supports the statement we mentioned on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr. Mention who said that. Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad Al-Qatwani told us: Zaid bin Habbab told us: Ayyash bin Uqba told me: Jabir bin Naim told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The even number is two days, and the odd number is one day. The correct thing to say about this is: God Almighty swore by the even and the odd, and He did not specify one type of even or odd over another type by report or reason. Every even and odd is among what He swore by, and what the people of interpretation said was included in this division, due to the generality of His oath by that. The reciters differed in their recitation of the phrase and the Witr. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, recited it with a kasra on the waw. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two widely known readings in the readings of the regions, and two well-known languages among the Arabs, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.
89:4: And his saying: And the night when it departs means: And the night when it departs and goes away, it is said from it: So-and-so departed at night, departing when he departs. Some of them said: What he meant by his saying: And the night when it departs is the night of Jumu’ah, which is the night of Zudalifah. And in a similar manner to what Al-Dhaith said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Umar ibn Qays told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Mutarafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, And the night when it departs until some of it passes over some of it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: Ai told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the night when it departs, meaning: when it goes away. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, And the night when it departs, he said: when it departs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah: And the night when it departs. He said: And the night when it departs. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the night when it departs, meaning: when it departs. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And the night when it departs, he said: When it departs. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, regarding His statement, And the night when it departs, he said: The night when it departs. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah: And the night when it departs. He said: The night of Friday. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Syria and Iraq read it as yusr without the yaa, while a group of reciters read it with the yaa. The yaa was omitted in this ajba ilaina to reconcile the beginnings of the verses if they were with the raa. The Arabs sometimes omitted the yaa in the nominative case like this, making do with the kasra before it. An example of this is the saying of the poet. My wealth is not hidden as much as the day I was born. My poverty is not hidden as much as my nature.
89:5: And His statement: Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? God Almighty says: Is there any satisfaction in what I have sworn by regarding these matters for one of understanding? What He meant by that is: Indeed, in this oath is sufficient for one who understands about his Lord. He is more severe in oaths. As for the meaning of his saying of sound mind, he is of sound mind and intellect. It is said of a man who is the master of himself, subduing and controlling himself: he is of sound mind. From this comes their saying: the ruler has control over so-and-so. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Kurayb and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, of a person of wisdom, he said: of a person of a river and reason. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, For those with reason, he said: For those with understanding. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: Ai told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Is there in that an oath for one of reason? He said: One of reason, understanding, and intellect. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhibyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A portion for the one with reason. He said: for the one with intelligence, for the one with understanding. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Aghar Al-Manqari, on the authority of Khalifa bin Al-Hussain, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A portion for the one with reason. He said: for the one with intelligence, for the one with wisdom. Muhammad bin Amr urged me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Is there in that an oath for one of reason? He said: For one of reason. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: One with reason, one with opinion. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, Is there in that an oath for one who has reason? He said: For one who has intelligence, or prohibition. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Hilal bin Khabab, on the authority of Mujahid regarding Qaluh: An oath for the one with reason. He said: For the one with intelligence. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan: Is there in that an oath for one who has reason? He said: For one who has patience. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, of one with reason, he said: of one with intelligence. Al-Hasan said: of one with understanding. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Is there in that an oath for one of reason? for one of reason, one of intellect and mind. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Is there in that an oath for one of reason? He said: For one of reason. And he read, For a people who understand (al-Jathiyah 45:5) and for those of understanding, and they are those whom God rebuked and said: Reason and reason are one, except that they differ in the speech of the Arabs.
89:6: And His saying: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the ‘Ad tribe * Iram? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not looked, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart and seen how your Lord dealt with the ‘Ad tribe?
89:7: The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of his saying Iram. Some of them said: It is the name of a town. Then those who said that differed in the town that was meant by that. Some of them said: It meant Alexandria. It was mentioned by the one who said that: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yaqub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of al-Qurazi, that he heard him say: Iram of the Pillars is Alexandria. Abu Jaafar said: Others said: It is Damascus. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hilali, one of the people of insight, told me: Ubaid God bin Abdul Majeed told us: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told us, on the authority of Al-Maqburi: A’ad * Iram of the pillars. He said: Damascus. Another said: What he meant by his saying Iram is a nation. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amara told me: Ubaid bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Iram, he said: A nation. Others said: It means: old. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Iram, he said: the ancient. Others said: That is a tribe from Ad. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Ad, Iram, who had lofty pillars? He said: We used to think that Iram was a tribe of ‘Ad, the house of the queen of ‘Ad. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Iram, he said: A tribe from Ad, who were called Iram, the ancestor of Ad. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Ad * Iram? God says: With ‘Ad Iram, that ‘Ad is the son of Iram, the son of ‘Aws, the son of Sam, the son of Noah. Others said: Iram: the perishing. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the ‘Ad people? Iram. He means by Iram: the destroyed. Do you not see that you say: Iram, the sons of so-and-so? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Abad * Iram, that it means destruction. Do you not see that you say, Iram, the sons of so-and-so, meaning they were destroyed? The correct thing to say about this is that Iram was either a town that was usually inhabited, and therefore it was returned to Aad to follow it, and it was not declined for that reason, or it was the name of a tribe, and it was not declined either, just as the names of tribes such as Tamim and Bakr and the like are not declined if they mean the tribe. As for the name Aad, it was not declined, as it was a foreign name. As for what was mentioned on the authority of Mujahid, that he said: He meant by that the ancient, then this statement has a meaning for it, because if that was its meaning, it would have been reduced by the tanween, and in leaving out the procedure there is evidence that it is not an adjective or a description. The most correct of the sayings about it in my opinion is that it is the name of a tribe from Aad, and that is why the reading came without adding Aad to it, and without applying it, as one says: Have you not seen what your Lord did with Tamim Nahshal? So the application of Nahshal is left out, and it is a tribe, so it was left in its application for that reason, and it is in the accusative case in response to Taym. If Iram was the name of a town or the name of an ancestor of Aad, the reading would have come with the addition of Aad to it, as one says: This is Amr Zubayd, Hatim is Tayy, and A’sha is Hamdan. But it is the name of a tribe from it, in my opinion, as Qatada said: And God knows best. That is why the reciters agreed on it without adding it and without applying it. His saying: of the pillars. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying of the pillars in this place. Some of them said: Its meaning is: of height, and they went in that to the Arabs’ saying for a tall man: a pillared man, and they said: They were of tall bodies. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Of the pillars means: Their height is like pillars. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaid God bin Wasi told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of the pillars, he said: They had a body in the sky. Some of them said: Rather, they were called the people of pillars because they were people of pillars, seeking rain, moving to the grass wherever it was, then returning to their homes. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the pillar, he said: The people of the pillar do not stand. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Dhat al-Imad, he said: It was mentioned to us that they were people of pillars who did not stay, a caravan. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Dhat al-Imad, he said: They were the people of the pillar. Others said: Rather, this was said about a building that some of them built, so he erected its pillars and raised its building. Mention who said that. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Iram, of the lofty pillars, he said: Ad, the people of Hud, built it and climbed it when they were in Al-Ahqaf. He said: The like of it has not been created like those works in the land. He said: And likewise in Al-Ahqaf in Hadhramaut, then there were Ad. He said: And there are the sand dunes, as God said about the sand dunes, sands like mountains, forming a hollow canopy. Others said: This was said to them because of the strength of their bodies and their powers. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: There are slaves. He said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement of the pillars he means: strength and power. The most similar of the statements in this regard to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation is the statement of the one who said: What is meant by that is that they were people of a carved pillar, because what is known in the speech of the Arabs of the pillar is what tents are supported by from wood, and for the masts on which the building is supported, and there is no known building that they had with pillars by a sound report. Rather, the people of interpretation have directed his saying of the pillars to the fact that he meant by it the length of their bodies, and some of them to the fact that he meant by it the pillars of their tents. As for the pillars of the building, no one of the people of interpretation knows much about his direction of it, and the interpretation of the Qur’an is only directed to the most common and well-known of its meanings, for what is found a way to that, without the most reprehensible.
89:8: And His statement: The like of which had not been created in any land means God Almighty says: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram, the like of which had not been created in any land? He means: like 'Ad, and the ha' refers back to 'Ad. It is possible that it refers back to Iram, as we have previously explained that it is a tribe. What He meant by His statement: The like of which had not been created in size, power, and strength. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, The like of which has not been created in the lands, he mentioned that they were twelve cubits in length in the sky. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Of the pillars * The like of which has not been created in the land. The like of the pillars has not been created in the land. They said: The like of which has not been created in the description of the one with the pillars, and the ha in its thal is only from the mention of the one with the pillars. Mention who said that. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, Then he mentioned something similar. This is a baseless statement, because ‘Imad’ is a singular male, and ‘al-la’ is for the female, and the male is not described by ‘al-la’. If that were an attribute of ‘Imad, it would have been said: the one like which has not been created in the land. If ‘al-la’ was made for Iram, and the ‘ha’ was made to refer back in his statement like it to it, and it was said: it is Damascus or Alexandria, because the land of ‘Aad is the one described by God in His Book when He said: And remember the brother of ‘Aad when he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf (al-Ahqaf 46:21). Al-Ahqaf is the plural of ‘haqf’, which is the curved and bent part of the sand. Alexandria and Damascus are not from the lands of the sand, rather those trees are from the land of Hadhramaut and its environs.
89:9: And His statement: And Thamud who cut through the rocks in the valley, meaning: And Thamud who cut through the rocks and entered them, and made them homes, as God Almighty said: And they used to carve out homes from the mountains, feeling secure. (al-Hijr 15:82) The Arabs say: So-and-so cut through the desert, if he entered it and crossed it, and this is the statement of Nabigha. Abu Layla came to you, roaming the darkness, the darkness of the night, the path of the wilderness, What he means by his saying: He enters and cuts. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ali Y, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And Thamud who hewed out the rocks in the valley, he said: They tore them apart. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley. Meaning: Thamud, the people of Salih, used to carve houses out of the mountains. Muhammad bin Amara told me, he said: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Jahid, regarding his statement, Those who hewed out the rocks in the valley, he said: They hewed out the mountains and made them into houses. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley, they hewed them out and carved out houses from them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: They brought the rock means they dug into the rock. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They brought the rocks into the valley, that he said: They drove the stones. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, in his statement, And Thamud, who hewed out the rocks in the valley, they built houses and dwellings in the rocks in the mountains, until they made dwellings in them. They hewed out: they searched them, you searched out the houses in the mountains. Someone said: Everything except God will perish, just as the living, the dragon and the giant perish. They struck at every prayer Saada with strong hands and forearms
89:10: And His saying: And Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes, God Almighty says: Have you not seen how your Lord also dealt with Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes? The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying, Of the pegs, and when that was said to him, some of them said: The meaning of that is: of the soldiers who strengthened his command, and they said: The pegs in this context are the soldiers. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And Pharaoh of the stakes. He said: The stakes are the soldiers who testify for him. It is said: Pharaoh used to attach iron stakes to their hands and feet, to which he would hang them. Others said: Rather, he was called that because he used to peg people with pegs. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqaa Ju’i’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Of the stakes, he said: He used to peg people with stakes. Others said: They were tents and playgrounds where he could play. Mention who said that. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And Pharaoh, the lord of the stakes. He told us that it was a place of oppression and play for him under it, made of stakes and ropes. Ibn Abi Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Of the Stakes. He said: Of the buildings, there were shelters under which he played, and stakes that were struck for him. He said: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Thabit al-Banani, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, who said: Pharaoh pegged his wife with four pegs, then he placed a huge millstone on her back until she died. Others said: Rather, that was because he was torturing people with stakes. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Mahmoud, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr: And Pharaoh of the stakes means: He would place a man here and a man there, and a hand here, and with the stakes. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Of the Stakes, he said: He used to peg people with stakes. Others said: It was said that because he had a building that he used to torture people on. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, And Pharaoh of the stakes, he said: He had minarets on which he would torture them. The first of these sayings that is most correct in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by that is the pegs that are pegged, whether they are made of wood or iron, because that is the well-known meaning of pegs and they were described as such, because either he was torturing people with them, as Abu Rafi and Saeed bin Jubayr said, or he was playing with them.
89:11: And His statement: Those who transgressed in the land means by His statement, may His praise be exalted, those: Aad, Thamud, Pharaoh and his soldiers. And by His statement, transgressed means: they went beyond what their Lord had permitted them, and rebelled against their Lord by going to what He had forbidden them of disbelief in Him. And His statement, in the land: the ones they were in.
89:12: God the Almighty says: So they multiplied their sins in the land, and committed what God had forbidden them. So your Lord poured down upon them a scourge of punishment. God the Almighty says: So, O Muhammad, your Lord sent down His punishment upon them, and inflicted upon them His vengeance, because they spread corruption in the land, and rebelled against God therein. So your Lord poured down upon them scourges of punishment. The punishments that came down upon them were either a wind that destroyed them, or an earthquake that destroyed them, or drowning that destroyed them, without being struck with a whip or a stick, because one of the most painful punishments of the people addressed by this Qur’an was flogging with whips. So the people often used to describe the severity of the painful punishment with which a man was punished, by saying: So-and-so was flogged with whips, until it became a proverb, and they used it for anyone who was being punished with a severe type of punishment, and they said: A whip of punishment was poured upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.
89:13: His saying, A whip of torment. He said, What they were tormented with. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment, he said: The punishment with which He punished them, He called it: a scourge of punishment.
89:14: And His statement: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is ever watchful of those whose stories I have related to you, and of those like them among the disbelievers in Him. He is ever watchful of their deeds in this world and in the Hereafter, on the bridges of Hell, to pile them up in it when they enter it on the Day of Resurrection. The interpreters differed. Some of them said: The meaning of his saying on the lookout is that he sees and hears. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful, meaning: He sees and hears. Others said: He means that he is watching the people of injustice. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Mujahid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding this verse, he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the Lord will command His Throne to be placed on the Fire, and He will sit on it, then He will say: By My glory and majesty, no one with a wrong will surpass Me today. That is His saying, Ambushing. He said: Al-Hakam bin Bashir narrated to us, he said: Amr bin Qais narrated to us, he said: I have been informed that there are three bridges over Hell: a bridge over which is the trust, when they pass by it it says: O Lord, this is a trustworthy person, O Lord, this is a traitor. A bridge over which is the womb, when they pass by it it says: O Lord, this is one who maintains ties, O Lord, this is one who severs them. A bridge over which is the Lord: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. He said: Mahran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, Indeed, your Lord is watching. He means that Jahm has three bridges over him: a bridge in which is mercy, a bridge in which is trust, and in which is the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Hasan: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful. He said: He is ever watchful of the actions of the children of Adam.
89:15: And His statement: But as for man, when his Lord tests him, God Almighty says: But as for man, when his Lord tests him with blessings and wealth, then honors him with water, and favors him, and favors him with what He has bestowed upon him of His bounty, then he says, ‘My Lord has honored me,’ so he rejoices in that, and is pleased with it, and says, My Lord has honored me with this honor. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, But as for man, when his Lord tests him and honors him and blesses him, he says, ‘My Lord has honored me.’ And it is right for him.
89:16: And His statement: But if He tests him and restricts his provision, meaning: But if his Lord tests him with poverty, and restricts his provision, meaning: His provision is reduced and made scarce, so his wealth is not increased, nor is it expanded for him. Then he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me,’ meaning: That person says: My Lord has humiliated me, meaning: He has humiliated me with poverty, and he does not thank God for giving him soundness of his limbs and providing him with well-being in his body. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’ How quickly the son of Adam disbelieves. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, regarding His statement, He restricted his provision, he said: He restricted it. The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement, and He restricted his provision for him. The majority of reciters in the regions recited it with a light qadara meaning he became poor, except for Abu Ja`far al-Qari, who recited it with a shaddah fa qadara. It was reported on the authority of Abu `Amr ibn al-`Alaa that he used to say, qadara, meaning he would give him what would suffice him, and he would say, If He had done that to him, he would not have said, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’ The correct reading for us is to read it with a light pronunciation, as the authoritative reciters have agreed on it.
89:17: And His statement: No, but you do not honor the orphan. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement No in this place, and what He denied thereby. Some of them said: God, the Most High, denied that the reason for his honor was from the one who honored him because of his abundant wealth, and the reason for his humiliation was from the one who humiliated him because of his little wealth. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’ How quickly the son of Adam disbelieves! God Almighty says: No! I do not honor whom I honor with an abundance of this world, nor do I humiliate whom I humiliate with a scarcity of it. Rather, I honor whom I honor with obedience to Me, and I humiliate whom I humiliate with disobedience to Me. Others said: Yes, He, the Most High, denied that a person would praise his Lord for a blessing without his poverty, and complain of his need. They said: The meaning of the statement is: No, meaning it should not have been like this, but he should have praised Him for both matters, both for his wealth and his poverty. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion we mentioned from Qatada, because his statement, But you do not honor the orphan, and the verses that follow it indicate that he only humiliated the one who humiliated because he did not honor the orphan, nor encourage the feeding of the poor, and all the other meanings that he enumerated. And in his clarification of the reason for which he humiliated the one who humiliated, there is clear evidence of the reason for honoring the one who honored, and in his clarification of that following his statement, But as for man, when his Lord tests him and honors him and blesses him, he says, ‘My Lord has honored me.’ But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, ‘My Lord has humiliated me.’ This is a clear statement of what he denied in his statement what we have described. And His statement: Rather, you do not honor the orphan, God Almighty says: Rather, I have humiliated whomever I have humiliated because he does not honor the orphan. So He made the speech direct to the address, and said: Rather, you do not honor the orphan, and for that reason I have humiliated you.
89:18: His saying: And do not encourage one another to feed the poor. The reciters differed in the recitation of this. Abu Ja`far from Medina and the majority of the reciters from Kufa recitedبال ل َقهقُرونق اللذصينقwith the ta’ and fat-ha, and maintaining the alif, meaning: nor do they urge one another to feed the poor. Some of the reciters from Mecca and the majority of the reciters from Medina recited it with the ta’ and fat-ha, and deleted the alifل َقَقُرونقmeaning: nor do they order the feeding of the poor. The majority of the reciters from Basra recited يهقُرونقwith the ya’ and deleted the alif, meaning: nor do the ones who say when He afflicts him, may God have mercy on him, honor him and bless him, my Lord has honored me, and when He has decreed his provision for him, my Lord has humiliated me, the orphan, and nor do they urge one another to feed the poor. And those of Basra we mentioned also reciteيكرمرونقand the rest of the letters with it with the ya’, as a report from those we mentioned. It has been reported from some of them that they recitedيهقُرونقwith the ta’ and damma, and maintaining the alif, meaning: nor do they guard. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that these are well-known readings in the readings of the regions, I mean the three readings that are correct in meaning, so whichever of them the reader reads, he is correct.
89:19: And His statement: And you devour the inheritance, devouring it completely. God Almighty says in His remembrance: And you devour the inheritance, O people, devouring it completely, meaning: devour it intensely, you do not leave anything of it, and it is from their saying, I gathered what was on the table, so I gathered it completely: if you ate what was on me, so you finished all of it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Amr bin Saeed bin Yasar Al-Qurashi told me, he said: Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And you devour the inheritance, devouring it completely. He said: The inheritance. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And you consume the inheritance, meaning the inheritance. And likewise in His statement: Consuming what. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you devour inheritance with a devouring devotion. He says: You devour with a great devouring. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And you devour inheritance, devouring what it has. He said: And the share of its owner. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They ate what he said: The lam is the side, the wrapping of everything. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: He ate it intensely: meaning intensely. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, eating of what, that he said: eating intensely. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd, regarding His statement, And you devour inheritance, devouring what you find, he said: The devouring devourer is the one who ate everything he found without asking, so he ate what was his and what was his companion’s. They did not give women an inheritance, nor did they give children an inheritance. And he recited, “And they ask you about women. Say, ‘God gives you a legal opinion about them and what is recited to you in the Book about orphan women to whom you do not give what is prescribed for them and whom you desire to marry and about the weak among children.” (An-Nisa’: 127) meaning, you do not give them an inheritance either, devouring what you find, he eats his inheritance, and everything he does not ask about, and he does not know whether it is permissible or forbidden. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, You consume inheritance, devouring it in vain. He said: Through it. Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Amr ibn Abi Salamah al-Basti told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Salim, who said: I heard Bakr ibn Abd God say about this verse, And you devour inheritance, devouring what you have lost. He said: Devouring means transgression in inheritance, devouring one’s inheritance and the inheritance of others.
89:20: God Almighty means by His saying, And you love money with an overwhelming love, and you love to collect money, O people, and to acquire it with an intense, great love, from their saying: The water has accumulated in the pool, meaning it has gathered together. And from this is the saying of Zuhair ibn Abi Salma: When they reached the blue water, they put down the sticks of the campers. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And you love wealth with an intense love, he said: intensely. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And you love wealth with an excessive love, meaning they love an abundance of wealth. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, a great deal of love, he said: A great deal means a lot. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And you love wealth with an intense love: meaning, an intense love. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, with abundant love, that they love an abundance of money. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Yazid said, regarding His statement, And you love wealth with an intense love, he said: Excessive means intense.
89:21: And by His saying, No, He, the Most High, means that this is not how things should be. Then He, the Most High, informed us of their regret for their bad deeds in this world, and their longing for what they did in the past when regret will be of no use to them, so He, the Most High, said, No! When the earth is pounded to powder, meaning: when it returns and is shaken with a violent earthquake, and moves one movement after another. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, No! When the earth is pounded to powder, meaning: It is moved. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yaharmala bin Imran told me, that he heard Umar, the freed slave of Ghafra, say: If you hear God say, No, then He is only saying, You have lied.
89:22: And His saying: And your Lord will come with the angels, rank upon rank. God Almighty says: And when your Lord comes, O Muhammad, with His angels, rank upon rank. Ibn Bashar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, on the authority of Abu al-Munhal, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched out like a leather cover, and its width will be increased to such and such, and all creation will be gathered together on one plain, their jinn and their humans. Then, when that day comes, this lowest heaven will be taken away from its inhabitants on the face of the earth, and the inhabitants of the heaven alone will have twice as many jinn and humans as the inhabitants of the earth. When they are scattered over the face of the earth, they will be terrified by them and will say, 'Is our Lord among you?' They will be terrified by what they say and will say, 'Glory be to our Lord! He is not among us!' And He is coming. Then the second heaven will be taken away, and the inhabitants of the second heaven alone will have twice as many jinn and humans as the inhabitants of the lowest heaven and all the inhabitants of the earth. When they are scattered over the face of the earth, the inhabitants of the earth will be terrified by them and will say, 'Is our Lord among you?' They will be terrified by what they say and will say: Glory be to our Lord! He is not with us! And He is coming! Then the heavens will be judged, one by one. Whenever a heaven is judged for its inhabitants, it will be more numerous than the inhabitants of the heavens below it, and more numerous than all the inhabitants of the earth by a factor of two. Then when they are scattered over the face of the earth, the inhabitants of the earth will be terrified by them and say the same to Him, and they will return to them the same, and they will return to them the same, until the seventh heaven is judged. So the inhabitants of the seventh heaven will have more inhabitants than the inhabitants of six heavens, and more numerous than all the inhabitants of the earth by a factor of two. Then God will come to them while the people are kneeling in rows, and a caller will call out: Today you will know who are the companions of the vineyard. Let those who praise God in every circumstance stand up. They will be strengthened and set out for Paradise. Then a second call will be made: Today you will know who are the companions of the vineyard. Where were their sides turning away from their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spending from what We have provided them? Then he will call out a third time: You will know today who are the companions of generosity, meaning those who are not distracted by trade or sale from the remembrance of God, establishing prayer, and giving zakat. Do they fear a Day when hearts and eyes will be overturned? Then they will rise and be directed to Paradise. When three of these are taken, he will emerge from the Fire and look down upon creation. He has two eyes that see and a tongue that speaks clearly. He will say: “I have been entrusted with three of you: with every stubborn tyrant, who will pick them up from the rows as a bird picks up sesame seeds, and will detain them in Hellfire.” Then he will call out a third. Awf said: Abu al-Munhar said: “I thought he was saying: ‘I have been entrusted with the companions of the pictures, who will pick them up from the rows as a bird picks up sesame seeds, and will detain them in Hellfire.’ When three of these are taken, the scrolls will be spread out, the scales will be set up, and creation will be called to account.” Musa bin Abd al-Rahman told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of al-Ajlah, who said: I heard al-Dahhak bin Zahim say: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will command the lowest heaven with its inhabitants, and the angels in it will descend, and they will surround the earth and whoever is on it, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth, then the sixth, then the seventh, and they will be arranged in rows below each other. Then the highest angel will descend on his left side, Hell. When the people of the earth see it, they will call out, and they will not come to any region of the earth except that they will find seven rows of angels, so they will return to the place they were in. This is what God says: Indeed, I fear for you the Day of Calling * The Day you will turn back, fleeing, having no protector from God (Ghafir 40:32-33), and this is what God says: And your Lord will come with the angels, rank upon rank, and Hell will be brought forth that Day and His statement: “O company of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass. You will not pass except by authority” (al-Rahman 55:55). 33] This is what God says: And the heaven will be split open, and that Day it will be fragile, and the angels will be over its sides. (al-Haqqah 69:16-17) Abu Kurayb narrated: Abdur-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Muharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafi’ al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You will stand in one place on the Day of Resurrection for a period of seventy years. No one will look at you and no judgment will be passed between you. You will be stopped, and you will weep until your tears stop, then you will shed tears of blood, and you will weep until it reaches your chins, or you will be restrained and you will groan. Then you will say: ‘Who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that He may judge between us?’ They will say: ‘Who is more deserving of that than your father?’ God made his soil and created him with His hand, and breathed into him of His spirit, and made him all a child. Then Adam, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be brought and asked to do that, and he will come. Then the prophets will be brought, one by one, and every time they come to a prophet, he will refuse.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Until they come to me. When they come to me, I will go out until I come to the examination.” Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of God, what is the examination? He said: In front of the Throne. So I prostrated, and I remained prostrating until God sent an angel to me, and he took hold of my arm and lifted me up. Then God said to me: Muhammad, and He knows best. I said: Yes. He said: What is the matter with you? I said: O Lord, You promised me intercession, so grant me intercession for Your creation and judge between them. He said: I have accepted your intercession. I will come to you and judge between you. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: So I turned and stood with the people. While we were standing, we heard a loud noise from the sky, and we were stunned. Then the people of the lowest heaven descended with the same number as those on earth, of jinn and humans, until when they came close to the earth, the earth shone with their light, and they took hold of their ranks, and we said to them: Is our Lord among you? They said: No, and He is coming. Then the people of Heaven will descend, twice as many as those who descended from the angels, and twice as many as those who are in it from the jinn and mankind, until when they come near the earth, the earth will shine with their light, and they will take their places. We will say to them, Is our Lord among you? They will say, No, and He is coming. Then the inhabitants of the heavens descended in a measure of weakness, until the Almighty descended in the shadows of the clouds and the angels, and they had a voice from their glorification, saying: Glory be to the Possessor of the Kingdom and the Sovereignty, Glory be to the Lord of the Throne, the Possessor of the Mighty, Glory be to the Ever-Living Who does not die, Glory be to the One who causes the creation to die and does not die, Glory be to the Holy One, Lord of the angels and the Spirit, Holy is the Bow, Glory be to our Lord, the Most High, Glory be to the Possessor of the Mighty, the Sovereignty, the Pride, the Authority, and the Greatness, Glory be to Him, Forever and Ever. On that day, eight will carry His Throne, and today they are four, their feet on the borders of the lowest earth and the heavens to their sides, and the Throne is on their shoulders. Then God placed His Throne in a place He wanted on the earth, then He calls out with a call that the creation can hear, saying: O company of jinn and mankind, I have listened since the day I created you until this day, I hear your speech, and I see your deeds, so listen to Me, for these are your scrolls and your deeds that are read to you, so whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him not. They blame no one but themselves. Then God commands Hell, and a shining, dark neck emerges from it. Then God says, Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy? (Ya-Sin 36:60) until His saying, This is Hell, which you were promised. “And separate yourselves this Day, you criminals.” (Ya-Sin 36:59-63) So the people will be separated and kneel, and it is about this that God says, And you will see every nation kneeling, every nation will be called to its record today. (al-Jathiyah 45:28), and God will judge between His creation, the jinn, mankind, and animals. Indeed, He will punish the jinn with horns, until there is no longer any responsibility for one another, and God will say, Be dust. At that time, the disbeliever will say, Oh, I wish I were dust. Then God, the Exalted, will judge between the jinn and mankind. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his saying, And your Lord will come with angels, rank upon rank, the ranks of angels.
89:23: And His statement: And Hell will be brought forth on that Day. God Almighty says: And God will come and bring forth Hell. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Marwan Al-Fazari told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Khalid Al-Asadi, on the authority of Shaqiq bin Sala, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud said, regarding His statement, And Hell will be brought forth on that Day, he said: It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein being seventy thousand angels leading it. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hasan told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Abu Wa’il: And Hell will be brought forth on that Day. He said: It will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand reins, with each rein being led by seventy thousand angels. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: His two sides are Paradise and Hell. He said: When He descends from His Throne to His Chair, to judge His creation. And he recited: And Hell will be brought forth on that Day. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And Hell will be brought forth on that Day. He said: It will be brought forth bound. And His statement: On that Day man will remember, God Almighty says: On that Day man will remember his negligence in this world in obeying God and in doing good deeds that bring him closer to Him. And how will he be reminded? He says: From what point of view will he be reminded? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And how will he be reminded? He said: How will he be?
89:24: And His statement: “Oh, would that I had sent forth for my life,” God Almighty says, informing us of the eagerness of the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and indicating his negligence in performing righteous deeds in this life that would guarantee him eternal life in unending bliss: Oh, would that I had sent forth for my life in this world righteous deeds for this life of mine, after which there is no death, that which would save me from the wrath of God and would make him worthy of His pleasure. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Hudha told us, he said, Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, On that Day man will remember, but how will he receive remembrance? He will say, ‘Oh, would that I had sent forth for my life.’ He said: God knew that he was truthful, there is a long life in which there is no death in which the last thing upon him is death. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life. By God, there is a long life. Muhammad bin Aru told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life, he said: The Hereafter.
89:25: And His statement: On that Day no one will punish as He punishes, nor will anyone bind as He binds. The reciters of all regions agreed in their recitation of this by breaking the dhal of ya’dhu’dhu’ and the tha’ of yuthaq, except for Al-Kisa’i, who recited it by opening the dhal and the tha’, based on a report narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited it like this, but its chain of transmission is weak. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Kharijah, on the authority of Khalid Al-Hadha’, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: He told me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to him: On that Day no one will punish with His punishment. The correct statement in this regard in our view is that it is what the regions read, which is the kasra on the dhal and thā’, due to the consensus of the leading reciters on it. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: On that Day no one will be punished with the punishment of God in this world, and no one will be bound as he will be bound on that Day in this world. And that is how the reciters of that from the people of interpretation interpreted it. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On that Day no one will punish with His punishment, and no one will be bound as tightly as God binds. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Ma’ar, on the authority of al-Hasan: On that Day no one will be punished as He punished.
89:26: His saying: And no one will be bound as he is bound. He said: God knows that this world is torment and bondage, so He said: Then no one will be tormented as he is tormented in this world, and no one will be bound as he is bound in this world. As for the one who read it with the fat-ha, he directed its interpretation to: On that Day no one will be punished in this world as God will punish on that Day, and no one will be bound in this world as he will be bound on that Day. Some of the later scholars who read it with the fat-ha interpreted it as: On that Day no one will be punished as the disbeliever will be punished, and no one will be bound as the disbeliever will be bound. He said: How can the kasr be permissible, when there is no punisher on that Day except God? This is a wrong interpretation, because the people of interpretation interpreted it differently, despite the consensus of the authoritative reciters to read it with the meaning that the people of interpretation interpreted it with. I do not think that what prompted him to read it like that was his lack of a correct interpretation.
89:27: And His statement: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. God Almighty says, informing about what the angels will say to His friends on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:O reassured soul. By reassured soul, He means the one who is reassured by God’s promise that He promised the people of faith in this world of honor in the Hereafter, and so believes in that. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: O reassured soul, meaning: the one who believes. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: O reassured soul: he is the believer whose soul is reassured by what God has promised. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan, regarding His statement, O reassured soul, they said: Reassured by what God has said, and believing in what He has said. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: the one who believes and is certain that God is her Lord, and who submits to His command in what He does to her. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, O reassured soul, he said: The soul that is certain that God is its Lord, and has submitted to His command and obedience. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, O reassured soul, he said: It is certain that God is its Lord, and it submits to His command with all its might. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: O reassured soul, he said: The soul that is repentant, humble, and fearful, has become certain that God is its Lord, and has submitted to His command with all its might. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: O reassured soul, he said: It is certain that God is its Lord, and it is steadfast in its desire for His command. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, the one who is content, he said: the one who is humble and content with God. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: O reassured soul, he said: The one that has become certain that God is its Lord, and has submitted to His command with all its might. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid: O reassured soul, he said: The humble one. Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid: O reassured soul, he said: The one that is certain of meeting God and is prepared for Him. He mentioned that this is in Abu’s reading O you secure soul. He mentioned the story. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr told us, on the authority of Harun Al-Qari: He said: Hilal told me, on the authority of Abu Saykh Al-Hana’i, regarding Abu’s reading: O soul, secure and reassured. Al-Kalbi said: The secure one in this context means the believing woman. It was said: This is the angel’s saying to the servant when he leaves, giving him good report of his Lord’s pleasure with him, and preparing for him the honor He has prepared for him. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed, who said: O reassured soul was recited.
89:28: His saying, Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, was in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Bakr said, This is good. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The angel will say it to you at the time of death. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. He said this at the time of death. Then enter among My servants. He said this on the Day of Resurrection. Others said about this: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Usama bin Zaid, on the authority of his father, regarding His statement, O reassured soul, he said: It is like being given good tidings of Paradise at the time of death, on the Day of Assembly, and at the Resurrection. And His saying, Return to your Lord, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: This is report from God, may He be glorified, about what the angels said to the soul of the believer about the resurrection, to warn it that it would return to the body of its owner. They said: What is meant by return here is its owner. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: O reassured soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. He said: The reassured souls will return to the bodies on the Day of Resurrection.
89:29: I was told on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Then enter among My servants, that God will command the souls on the Day of Resurrection to return to the bodies and come to God as He created them the first time. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding this verse, Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, referring to the body. Others said: Rather, this is said to her at the time of death. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih: Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing. He said: This is about death. Then enter among My servants. He said: This is the Day of Resurrection. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the one we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak, that this will only be said to them when the souls are returned to the bodies on the Day of Resurrection, based on the meaning of His statement, So enter among My servants and enter My Paradise. The interpreters differed about the meaning of this. Some of them said: It means: So enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise. Mention who said that. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then enter among My servants, he said: Enter among My righteous servants, and enter My Paradise. Others said: The meaning of this is So enter into My obedience and enter My Paradise. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Na’im bin Damdam, on the authority of Muhammad bin Zahim, the brother of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim: So enter among My servants meaning: in My obedience. And enter My Paradise meaning: in My mercy. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra interpreted the meaning of his saying, So enter among My servants as: So enter My party. Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa interpreted this verse, O reassured soul, as meaning faith and belief in reward and futility. Return to your Lord, the angels say to them when they have been given their books in their right hands. Return to your Lord, to what God has prepared for you of reward. He said: It could be that you say to them something similar to this: They intend to return from this world to this place of return. He said: And you say to the man, Who are you? He says, From Mudari, so you say, Be from Taymimi or Qaysi, meaning you are from one of these two. So be is a connection. Likewise, returning is a connection, because one has returned to the Resurrection. So the command is in the sense of report, as if he said, O soul, you are satisfied and pleasing. It was narrated on the authority of some of the predecessors that he used to recite this: So enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise. Who said that? Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Abaan bin Abi Ayyash, on the authority of Sulayman bin Qatta, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he recited it So enter among My servant with monotheism. Khallad bin Aslam told me: Al-Nadr bin Samil told us, on the authority of Harun al-Qari, who said: Hilal told me, on the authority of Abu al-Shaykh al-Hana’i: So enter among My servant. And in al-Kalbi’s statement: So enter among My servant, and enter My Paradise, it means: The soul returns to the body. The correct reading of this is So enter among My righteous servants, meaning: So enter among My righteous servants, to provide the most reliable proof for it from among the reciters.
89:30: His saying: And enter my Paradise.
